title: A friend at Midnight
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Christian Religious Education; not yet checked by a CRE teacher; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The child narrates Luke 11:5-10: at midnight a man asks a friend for three loaves for a visitor, the friend says the door is locked, but gets up because the man keeps asking; ask, seek, knock: pray persistently.

floor.question: What do we ask for in "give us today our daily bread"?

representations: a locked door drawn at night
steps: The man asks a friend for three loaves.
Because he keeps asking, the friend gets up.
contexts: praying for a sick parent day after day

board.do: Draw a house at night with a locked door.

board.say: Why did the friend at last get up?

board.do: Wait for the child to say because he kept asking.

misconceptions.ask: Why did the friend at last get up and give the loaves?

listen_for: One short prayer is enough and we should not ask again
misconceptions.ask: What does the parable teach about prayer?
How many loaves did the man ask for?

listen_for: Yes, God is unwilling to help
misconceptions.ask: Is God like the friend in bed who did not want to get up?
misconceptions.repair: Read Luke 11:11-13: if earthly fathers give good gifts, how much more God. The lesson is persistence, not that God is unwilling.

checks.question: How many loaves did the man ask for?
What does the parable teach about prayer?
checks.answer: Keep praying and do not give up
